IS0 6596 specifies the characteristics of data interchange on 136 mm (5.25 in) flexible disk cartridges using two-frequency recording at 7 956 ftprad, 1,9 tpmm (46 tpi), on one side. IS0 6596/l specifies the dimensional, physical, and magnetic characteristics ,of the cartridge so as to provide physical interchangeability between data processing systems. Together with the labelling scheme specified in IS0 7665, IS0 6596/l and IS0 6596/2 provide for full data interchange between data processing systems.

plementation.

4 1 Scope and field of application
4.1

General requirements
Mode of recording

This part of IS0 6596 specifies the magnetic characteristics, the track layout, and a track format to be used on a 130 mm (5.25 in) flexible disk cartridge, recorded at 7 956 ftprad on one side using two-frequency recording at a track density of 1,9 tracks per millimetre (tpmm) [46 tracks per inch (tpi)], which is intended for data interchange between data processing systems.
NOTE - Numeric values in the SI and/or Imperial measurement system in this International Standard may have been rounded off and therefore are consistent with, but not exactly equal to, each other. Either system may be used, but the two should be neither intermixed nor re-converted. The original design for this part of IS0 6596 was made using SI units.

The mode of recording shall be two-frequency where the start of every bit cell is a clock flux transition. A ONE is represented by a data flux transition between two clock flux transitions. Exceptions to this are defined in 4.10.

Characters shall be represented by means of the 7-bit coded character set (see IS0 646) and, where required, by its 7-bit or &bit extensions (see IS0 2022) or by means of the &bit coded character set (see IS0 4873). Each 7-bit coded character shall be recorded in bit-positions 87 to Bl of a byte; bit position 88 shall be recorded with bit ZERO. The relationship shall be as shown in figure 4. Each &bit coded character shall be recorder in bit-positions 68 to Bl of a byte. The relationship shall be as shown in figure 5.

7.2

Good

and bad tracks

A good track is a track which has been formatted according to 7.3. A bad track is a track which has been handled according to 7.4.

These two bytes shall be generated as defined in 4.11 using the bytes of the data block starting with the 7th byte of the data mark (see 6.4.1) and ending with the last byte of the data field (see 6.4.2).

Track 00 shall always be a good track. There shall be at least 32 good tracks from track 01 to track 34.

Annex

A tracks

Use of additional

(This annex does not form part of the standard.) IS0 6696 specifies the requirements for those tracks used for full data interchange, i.e., tracks 00 to 34, Additionally, tracks 35 to 39 may be used for purposes not requiring full data interchange. Dimension I, is sufficient to give access to 40 tracks. For these applications, the text of the following clauses of IS0 6536/l and IS0 6%6/2 IS0 6!XW 1 8.1.1 Number of tracks shall read :

There shall be 46 discrete concentric tracks in the recording area (6.3.4). In the following two sub-clauses, the figure 34 shall ba replaced by 39: 8.1.3.1 8.1.4 IS0 65X/2 In the following sub-clauses, the figure 32 shall be replaced by 37: 6.2.2.1 7.3.2.2.1 Track address (T) Track address (Tl Nominal locations Track number

Annex B EDC implementation
(This annex does not form part of the standard.) Figure 6 shows the feedback connections of a shift register which may be used to generate the EDC bytes. Prior to the operation, all positions of the shift register are set to ONE. Input data are added (exclusive OR) to the contents of position Cts of the register to form a feedback. This feedback is in its turn added (exclusive OR) to the contents of position C4and position Ctt. On shifting, the outputs of the exclusive OR gates are entered respectively into positions Cc, C s and C12. After the last data bit has been added, the register is shifted once more as specified above. The register then contains the EDC bytes. If further shifting is to take place during the writing of the EDC bytes, the control signal inhibits exclusive OR operations. To check for errors when reading, the data bits are added into the shift register in exactly the same manner as they were during writing. After the data, the EDC bvtes are also entered into the shift register as if they were data. After the final shift, the register contents will be all ZERO if the record does not contain errors.

Annex C Procedure and equipment for measuring flux transition spacing

(This annex does not form part of the standard.)

C.l

General

This annex specifies equipment and a procedure for measuring flux transition spacing on 130 mm (5.25 in) flexible disk cartridges using two-frequency recording at 7 958 ftprad on one side.

C.2

Format

The disk to be measured shall be written by the disk drive for data interchange use. Testing shall be done on tracks 00 and 34. The test patterns 001ooooO (20) and 11101111 (EF) shall be written repeatedly on each test track. Testing shall be done on tracks 00 and 34.

C.3
C.3.1

Test equipment
Disk drive

The disk drive shall have a rotational speed of 300 r/min, with a tolerance of f 3 r/min, averaged over one revolution. The average angular speed taken over 64 ps shall not deviate by more than 0,5 % from the speed averaged over one revolution. C.3.2 C.3.2.1 Head Resolution

The head shall have an absolute resolution of 55 % to 65 % at track 34, using the reference material RM 6566, applying the calibration factor of the reference material, and recording with the test recording current. The resonant frequency of the head shall be at least 250 Ooo Hz. The resolution shall not be adjusted by varying the load impedance of the head. The resolution shall be measured at the output of the amplifier defined in C.3.3.1.

j
I

C.3.2.2

Offset angle

The head shall have a gap offset angle of 0" f 6' with the disk radius on the testing drive. C.3.2.3 Contact

Care shall be taken that the head is in good contact with the media during the tests. C.3.3 C.3.3.1 Read channel Read amplifier 1 dB, and amplitude saturation shall not occur.

The read amplifier shall have a flat response from 1 Ooo Hz to 187 500 Hz within f C.3.3.2 Peak sensing amplifier

Peak sensing shall be carried out by a differentiating and limiting amplifier. 11

IS : 11404 (Part 2)-1986 IS0 6596/2-l 985

C.3.4

Time interval measuring

equipment

The time interval counter shall be able to measure 4 us to at least 10 ns resolution. A triggering oscilloscope may be used for this purpose.

C.4 C.4.1

Procedure

for measurement

Flux transition spacing measurement

The transition location shall be measured by the location of the peaks in the signal when reading. The flux transition spacing shall be measured by the pulse timing intervals after the read channel amplifier defined in C.3.3. C.4.2

Flux transition spacing

Measure time intervals tl to ra as shown in figure 7.
